thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for router service in eu-west-2 — p99 latency > 3s for 12m, streaming stalls observed. Paging sla: oncall-sre.

alec-ops: paging @sasha-oncall and @maya-sre — seeing p95 jump too. Users reporting partial streaming stalls (clients stuck at initial tokens).

sasha-oncall: I’m on it. grabbing traces and tail logs now. any customer hits? @lina-cs?

lina-cs: CX: a handful of customers (3) on Dedicated reported degraded response times; one customer reported timeouts during streaming sessions. CS has opened support cases, flagging high revenue customer.

maya-sre: quick telemetry: router ingress p50 ~120ms, p95 ~900ms, p99 ~3.6s. egress queue lengths spiking on a subset of router pods. Partitioned by routing-policy=eu-heavy.

devon-runtime: interesting — we see a small fraction of shards getting 5-10x request concentration (hot partition). KV cache hit rate still normal. Could be routing skew. pulling routing table diff.

raj-eng: adding context: we rolled policy rollout v2 three hours ago that adjusts small-weight fallback routing to prefer lower-cost pool. Might be related.

alec-ops: can you paste the policy rollout id?

raj-eng: rollout id = rollout/2026-03-15-eu-weight-adjust. Patch changes: prefer pool-east-2/low-cost for models with <10ms delta.

devon-runtime: copying routing table snapshot. Affected router instances have heavy affinity toward pool-east-2 even for eu-west-2 origin traffic — looks like a region tag mismatch in policy evaluation. This will create cross-region egress and queueing.

sasha-oncall: that matches heatmap — inbound -> routed to remote pool -> longer network RTT -> then backpressure in router -> tail latency. Any evidence of hotkey or single tenant?

maya-sre: request distribution: 92% of the spike is coming from one tenant prefix (cust-984) and a handful of high-rate sessions (streaming). So it's a combination: misrouting + hot tenant.

emily-product: cust-984 is the one who reported streaming timeouts. They were running high-concurrency streaming tests earlier.

devon-runtime: reproduction command: 
```
$ curl -H 'x-customer-id: cust-984' -X POST https://router.eu-west-2.redwood.local/generate -d @prompt.json
```
Observing consistent long tails when our policy evaluator returns pool-east-2 as candidate. Policy eval log: "preferred_pool: pool-east-2 (cost_delta -0.2)" — but region_priority check incorrectly treats region code 'eu-w' as matching 'eu-west-2' vs 'eu-west-2a' aliasing bug.

raj-eng: confirming: a tokenization bug in the rollout matcher caused substring match on region tag. PR #4512 attempted to improve fuzzy matches and introduced the aliasing. Rolling policy created affinity to wrong pool.

sasha-oncall: mitigation options? we need fast mitigation to reduce p99 and stop customer timeouts.

maya-sre: immediate: revert the policy rollout (safe) or temporarily pin routing for cust-984 to local pool. Which is faster?

raj-eng: revert rollout via rollout system ~2-3m to take effect cluster-wide. Pinning single tenant via config flag is also quick but requires updating routing controller and pushing to routers (~5-10m).

alec-ops: do rollback — low blast radius. execute now. @devon-runtime, start the rollback and monitor.

devon-runtime: starting rollback: 
```
$ rollout rollback rollout/2026-03-15-eu-weight-adjust --env=prod --region=eu-west-2
```
Triggered at 1768891358. Watching health checks.

incident-bot: Rollback job queued (job-id 79231). Estimated propagation 3-6m.

maya-sre: telemetry: p99 dropping from 3.6s -> 2.1s after 120s, still above SLO but improving. Some router pods still draining.

sasha-oncall: additionally, temporarily lower routing concurrency limit for streaming sessions on affected routers to reduce queueing: setting router.max_stream_concurrency=8 -> 5 for eu-west-2.

devon-runtime: applied concurrency change on edge-router-euw pods via k8s patch. pods restarted gracefully. effect visible after 60s.

maya-sre: p95 back to 400-600ms, p99 ~1.5s. Streaming stalls mostly resolved but a few sessions remain stuck; investigating session state.

lina-cs: CS confirming no new errors from cust-984 for last 10m. Case updated: customer-side retry suggested as short-term.

emily-product: are we confident this won't recur when rollout re-applies? We need postmortem and gating.

raj-eng: root cause: rollout matcher fuzzy region aliasing introduced substring match; combination with skewed traffic from cust-984 created hot cross-region routing and increased network RTT + router queue buildup. Fix: revert fuzzy-match behavior, add strict region equality check, add unit tests for region aliasing.

devon-runtime: also recommend telemetry guard: if cross-region egress rate > 5% and p99 > 1.5s, auto-fallback to local pool. Implementing an emergency guard in routing controller as a short-term patch.

alec-ops: can you open an incident ticket and assign owners? I'll create the incident page. Include: timeline, metrics, customer impact, mitigation, follow-ups.

sasha-oncall: creating incident doc -> https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026-0315-routing-friction (draft). Adding links to logs and rollbacks.

incident-bot: Deployment event: rollback rollout/2026-03-15-eu-weight-adjust -> successful (job-id 79231) at 1768891484.

maya-sre: after rollback stabilization (10m window): p99 at 0.9s, p95 300ms. streaming stalls resolved. marking incident severity: Sev2 -> customer impact limited to 3 customers and short duration ~25m.

emily-product: Product asks for communication: send a short postmortem to impacted customers with summary and reassurance that fix is in progress. @lina-cs coordinate messaging.

lina-cs: will draft emails and share. ETA 30m.

raj-eng: follow-ups (owner tags):
- raj-eng: fix matcher code, PR + tests, target deploy in next patch window (owner)
- devon-runtime: add emergency guard in routing controller, canary in eu-west-2 (owner)
- maya-sre: create alert rule for cross-region egress % + p99 threshold (owner)
- alec-ops: update runbook for routing rollbacks (owner)
- lina-cs: communicate to customers (owner)

sasha-oncall: handing off to night oncall @maya-sre. summary for handoff:
- root cause: fuzzy region aliasing in policy matcher -> cross-region routing to pool-east-2, hot tenant amplified tail.
- mitigations applied: rollout rollback, decreased streaming concurrency on affected routers, monitoring.
- current status: stabilized, p99 ~0.9s, no new errors from impacted customers in 20m.
- follow-ups assigned and tracked in incident doc.

maya-sre: acknowledging handoff. I’ll watch during the night and will escalate if we see p99 > 1.2s or cross-region egress > 3%.

alec-ops: thanks all. Good job on quick rollback and targeted mitigations. Please record timeline and signal in postmortem when PRs are ready. :thumbsup:

devon-runtime: clipped log snippet for root cause: 
```
[policy_eval] req_id=abc123 region_tag='eu-west-2a' candidate='pool-east-2' match_rule='fuzzy_region_alias' score=0.87
```

raj-eng: PR#4519 opened to change matcher to strict compare + add tests (link in incident doc).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315 transitioned to MONITORING at 1768892050.
